items.answer: Augmented reality (AR) is an enhanced version of reality created by technology, in which computer-generated digital content is overlaid on the real world in real time and registered in 3D, so the user perceives and interacts with the enhanced environment.

Virtual reality (VR) is an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli provided by a computer, in which a person's actions partially determine what happens and which replaces the user's sense of reality without requiring the physical existence of objects or places.

A virtual reality system is a system that presents a computer-generated artificial environment, provides computer-generated sensory stimuli for an immersive experience, and lets the user's actions partially determine what happens in it.
Visual motion is the movement experienced by a user in a virtual reality environment, and it is a virtual reality content factor that can increase the risk and severity of cybersickness.
A computer is one of the major components of virtual reality (VR) hardware, a device that processes data from input sensors and activates output devices so that a user can perceive the world.

An output device is an XR hardware component that produces output to stimulate a user's sensory organs, not only a visual display; examples include visual displays, audio output, haptics, motion platforms, and treadmills.

questions.question: Which virtual reality input method captures a user's voice and other audio for interaction?
options: Sound-based tracking
Head tracking
Camera-based tracking
Eye tracking
questions.explanation: Sound-based tracking uses microphones or microphone arrays to capture voice, speech, and non-speech sound. The other options track visual or head movement rather than audio.

questions.question: What makes full-body tracking able to strengthen a user's sense of embodiment in a virtual world?
options: A fuller representation of themselves
Gaze points recorded by eye trackers
Reflective markers on the user's suit
Voice captured by microphone arrays
questions.explanation: Full-body tracking supports embodiment and social presence by giving the user a fuller representation of themselves. Marker-based inference is a tracking method, and audio or gaze capture does not show the user's body.

questions.question: How does a MOCAP full-body tracking system obtain the user's body movement?
options: Suit sensors transmit raw movement data
Surrounding cameras infer movement from reflective markers
Eye trackers record gaze points for interaction
Microphone arrays capture audio in a 360-degree environment
questions.explanation: A MOCAP suit contains sensors that capture and transmit raw movement data, which is then combined into full-body position and movement. Cameras, microphones, and eye trackers describe other tracking or input methods.

data.text: Full-body and sound-based tracking are among the non-hand VR input methods alongside head and eye tracking. Full-body tracking goes beyond the head, hands, and eyes, and can strengthen the feeling of a fuller self and social presence in a virtual world. It is realized through motion capture suits or camera systems that read fiducial markers. Sound-based tracking is a separate input route that uses simple microphones or microphone arrays to capture speech and non-speech sound for interaction.
points: Non-hand VR input methods consist of head, eye, full-body, and sound-based tracking.
Full-body VR tracking tracks the whole body and can add to the illusion of self-embodiment and social presence.
Full-body VR tracking approaches are motion capture suits and camera-based fiducial-marker tracking.
Sound-based VR tracking captures voice, speech, and non-speech sound for interaction using simple microphones or microphone arrays.

questions.question: What is the role of the processing part in a VR system?
options: Processes input-sensor data and actuates output devices
Filters sensor noise and powers the display hardware
Tracks user movement and sends the measurement stream
Stores input-sensor data and displays the virtual scene
questions.explanation: The processing part works on data from input sensors and uses the result to actuate output devices. Storing, displaying, or merely sending measurements is not its stated role.

questions.question: What should determine the choice of a VR system's processing element?
options: The headset display, audio hardware, tracking accuracy, battery life, and sensor range
The application, target users, assumed devices and their availability, and required immersion
The room size, network bandwidth, user age, game genre, and preferred seating
The GPU speed, CPU core count, RAM size, storage capacity, and available network bandwidth
questions.explanation: The processing element is chosen based on the application, users, input and output devices, and the needed level of immersion. Component specifications alone are not the selection criteria.

questions.question: Why is a GPU especially useful for realistic VR experiences?
options: Its input interface reads user movements more directly
Its parallel processing speeds up complex rendering
Its larger memory lets it store more complex scenes
Its engine support creates the virtual environment on its own
questions.explanation: GPUs speed up rendering because rendering itself has a parallel structure that GPUs can exploit. Storage, sensor reading, and environment creation are not the reason.

questions.question: Why can a CPU-only VR processing system with minimal GPU support have problems?
options: The XR engine has many other tasks, so development can slow
The CPU has many other tasks, so performance can suffer
The GPU has many other tasks, so rendering can lag
The RAM has many other tasks, so storage can fail
questions.explanation: Modern CPUs are powerful, but they also handle many other tasks, so a VR system with little GPU support can have performance issues. The concern is tied specifically to the CPU's workload.

questions.question: When planning VR hardware, why does the choice of XR engine matter?
options: Each XR engine requires its own kind of input sensor
Each XR engine requires its own kind of head-mounted display
Each XR engine has its own minimum RAM requirement
Each XR engine requires its own kind of audio output
questions.explanation: An XR engine is middleware for developing and rendering VR experiences, and each one has its own minimum RAM requirement. Engine choice does not specify a particular display, sensor, or audio output.

data.text: A VR system uses a computer to process sensor data and drive output devices, and that computer can be a PC, workstation, distributed system, or smartphone depending on the application, users, devices, and immersion. The GPU, CPU, and RAM determine performance: GPUs and multi-GPU systems support complex rendering, multicore CPUs increase processing capacity, and GPU support is preferable to CPU-only processing. An XR engine provides the middleware needed to support, develop, and render VR experiences, with at least 8 GB RAM typically preferable for a good user experience.
points: In a VR system, the computer processes input sensor data and activates output devices.
VR computer choices include PC, workstation, distributed system, or smartphone, based on application, users, device availability, and immersion.
A VR computer's major components are the GPU, CPU, and RAM.
In VR, GPUs and multi-GPU systems accelerate rendering, multicore CPUs increase capacity, and GPU support is preferable to CPU-only.
Each XR engine is middleware for VR experiences; at least 8 GB RAM is typically preferable for VR hardware.

questions.question: Which VR sensory output systems are considered premature and mostly limited to specialized or research environments?
options: Haptic touch systems
Audio output systems
Motion platform systems
Taste and smell systems
questions.explanation: Taste and smell output systems are premature, not widely used, available, or popular, and are mostly confined to highly specialized environments or research domains.

questions.question: What distinguishes a world-fixed visual display from a head-mounted display?
options: The display surface remains fixed while the user moves in a physical space
The display surface is worn on the head and moves with the user
The display surface is a handheld screen carried by the user
The display surface is a small screen placed directly in front of the eyes
questions.explanation: A world-fixed display renders graphics on a surface or screen that does not move with the user's head, so the user can move within the physical space while the display itself stays fixed. The wrong options describe head-mounted or handheld displays.

questions.question: Even though an HMD can track head motion, why is it mainly treated as an output device in a VR system?
options: Its main use is to create spatial audio for the ears
Its main use is to process tracking data for the computer
Its main use is to place images directly in front of the user's eyes
Its main use is to provide touch feedback to the hands
questions.explanation: An HMD can be used as input for head motion, but its primary use is as a display device; it places images directly in front of the user's eyes.

questions.question: Which type of HMD is typically used for augmented virtuality, where real-world imagery appears inside a virtual environment?
options: Non-see-through HMDs
Optical see-through HMDs
Video see-through HMDs
Stereoscopic HMDs
questions.explanation: Video see-through HMDs are typically used for augmented virtuality because they bring real-time images or videos of the real world into an artificial or virtual environment. Non-see-through HMDs are typically for VR, optical see-through HMDs for AR, and stereoscopic viewing is a separate HMD feature.

data.text: VR output devices include visual displays, audio, haptics, motion systems, and mostly specialized taste and smell outputs. Visual displays are divided into head-mounted, world-fixed, and regular displays. Head-mounted displays bring screens close to the eyes, world-fixed displays keep graphics on stationary surfaces while the user moves, and regular displays are ordinary mobile or stationary screens often used for augmented reality.
points: VR output devices include visual displays, audio, haptics, motion systems, and mostly specialized taste and smell outputs.
Visual displays stimulate the eyes and are head-mounted, world-fixed, or regular displays.
Head-mounted displays put screens directly before the eyes and can be non-see-through, optical, or video see-through.
World-fixed displays render graphics onto fixed screens, such as monitors or caves, while the user moves.
Regular displays are common tablets or smartphones, typically for non-immersive VR and mostly used for augmented reality.

questions.question: Why are headphones preferred for a fully immersive VR audio setup?
options: They let the sound source change as the head moves
They make the sound source louder over distance
They keep the sound source fixed relative to the room
They keep the sound source fixed in the surrounding space
questions.explanation: Headphones support fully immersive audio because the sound source can shift as the user moves their head. Fixed speakers do not update the perceived sound position in the same way.

questions.question: What marks a haptic device as active rather than passive?
options: Computer-controlled physical feedback
Worn objects that move with the user
Attached objects that stay fixed in the room
Static objects that match virtual shapes
questions.explanation: Active haptic devices give physical feedback under computer control, while passive haptic devices are static real-world objects that are not computer-controlled.

questions.question: Which haptic type gives the sense of limb movement and muscular resistance?
options: Shapes matched by static real objects
Vibrations applied to the skin surface
Forces applied to muscles and joints
Currents passed through the skin
questions.explanation: Proprioceptive force-based haptics work on muscles and joints to create a sense of limb movement and resistance. Tactile haptics instead stimulate the skin through vibration or electrical current.

questions.question: How can motion sickness caused by a VR motion platform be reduced?
options: By making the platform convey stronger acceleration and jerk
By choosing an active platform over a passive one
By increasing the conflict between visual motion and perceived real-world motion
By decreasing the conflict between visual motion and perceived real-world motion
questions.explanation: Motion sickness from a motion platform can be reduced by reducing the mismatch between what the user sees moving and what their body perceives. Increasing the mismatch or using more active control is not a stated way to reduce it.

questions.question: What does a treadmill provide in a VR output system?
options: The sense of touch while holding a virtual object
The sense of orientation while the body moves
The sense of gravity while moving through space
The sense of walking or running in place
questions.explanation: Treadmills give the feeling of walking or running in place by providing input to the feet or legs. Whole-body orientation and gravity are associated with motion platforms, and touch feedback comes from haptic devices.

data.text: Non-visual VR output devices add sound, touch, and physical movement to the visual display. Audio provides spatialized sound, while haptic systems create touch sensations through different control, sensation, and grounding approaches. Motion platforms and treadmills then give the user a sense of bodily motion, with passive designs often reducing motion sickness.
points: VR audio output can provide 3D audio, and headphones are preferred for fully immersive systems.
Haptic outputs activate touch sensation and are categorized as passive or active, tactile or proprioceptive, and self-grounded or world-grounded.
Motion platforms move the whole body, can cause motion sickness, and passive user-controlled ones likely reduce it.
Treadmills create the sense of walking or running in place; omnidirectional treadmills can be active or passive.

options: Audio output
Visual display
Haptic output
Microphone
items.reason: Visual displays, audio output, and haptic outputs are output devices for a VR experience; a microphone is used as input for sound-based tracking.

options: Graphics processing unit
Random access memory
Central processing unit
Graphics card
items.reason: A graphics processing unit, a central processing unit, and random access memory are the major components of the computer in a VR system; a graphics card is a display controller used for rendering.

options: Head-mounted display
World-fixed display
Regular display
Fish tank display
items.reason: Head-mounted, world-fixed, and regular displays are the three broad types of visual displays; a fish tank display is a specific early world-fixed display.

questions.question: Why can full-body tracking in virtual reality strengthen the sense of self-embodiment and social presence in a virtual world?
questions.reference_answer: Full-body tracking tracks full-body movement, more than the head, hands, and eyes. Its output can show the user a fuller representation of themselves. That fuller representation can add to the illusion of self-embodiment and social presence in a virtual world.

questions.question: Why is a graphics processing unit preferable for virtual reality processing even when modern central processing units are powerful?
questions.reference_answer: A graphics processing unit speeds up rendering because of its inherent parallel processing abilities and the inherent parallelism in the rendering process. Modern central processing units are powerful, but they have many other tasks to do. A CPU-only virtual reality processing system with minimal graphics processing unit support can therefore have performance issues.

questions.question: How do virtual reality and augmented reality differ in the head-mounted display type typically associated with each?
questions.reference_answer: Virtual reality is typically associated with non-see-through head-mounted displays, and augmented reality is typically associated with optical see-through head-mounted displays. Virtual reality completely replaces the user's sense of reality with a virtual environment, whereas augmented reality alters the ongoing perception of the real world.

questions.question: How do passive and active haptic devices differ?
questions.reference_answer: Haptic outputs can be categorized as passive versus active. Passive haptic devices are static real-world physical objects that match the shape of virtual objects and are not controlled by the computer, whereas active haptic devices are physical objects or physical feedback controlled by the computer that provide a sense of touch when interacting with virtual objects.
